logo_override.validation_detail: HTTP 200, content-type image/png, 8919 bytes, 180x180 and fully opaque (no alpha to bleed); canvas pixel audit mean luminance 194 with 73% light and 17% dark pixels, and rendered on white it shows the Whitley Fund's monarch-butterfly device in orange and black on a light tile, clearly legible

notes: The stored URL redirects: https://whitleyaward.org/apply/ 302s to https://whitleyaward.org/apply-for-conservation-funding/apply-for-a-whitley-award/. The Whitley Fund for Nature is a registered wildlife conservation charity and is the body that awards the Whitley Awards, so its own mark is correct under rule 2 and image_kind is official_logo. Hard case: the site's real logo is NOT a file. The header logo is a single 19415-byte INLINE svg inside , viewBox 0 0 100 69.59, with fill #ee7117 (the Fund's orange butterfly) plus near-black wordmark fills #020202/#0e0e0e/#0b0b0b/#0c0c0c/#070707/#0a0a0a/#0d0d0d - it combines the butterfly device and the 'Whitley Fund for Nature' wordmark in one path set, and inline SVG has no probeable URL. The rendered header contains ZERO elements and there is no CSS background logo, so the brief's step-1 img/og:image/JSON-LD lookups all come back empty here. I therefore took the file-backed copy of the same butterfly device. Probed and accepted /content/themes/whitleyaward.org/touch-icon-iphone-retina.png (200, image/png, 8919 B, 180x180, opaque, visually confirmed). Probed and rejected: /content/themes/whitleyaward.org/touch-icon-ipad-retina.png (200, 8218 B, 167x167 - same artwork, smaller); /content/themes/whitleyaward.org/touch-icon-iphone.png, touch-icon-ipad.png and touch-icon-iphone-retina.png at the other declared sizes (200, smaller still); /content/themes/whitleyaward.org/favicon.ico (200, image/x-icon, 1150 B but only a 16x16 frame, mean luminance 67 - too small to render as a record image); /content/themes/whitleyaward.org/assets/images/logo.svg (404); /content/themes/whitleyaward.org/images/logo.png and /content/themes/whitleyaward.org/logo.png (both request timeouts, no bytes returned, so not usable); the og:image on the apply page, which points at standfirst-whitleyaward-production.imgix.net and is a photo of a Brazilian tree frog finalist - an imgix CDN mirror and a photograph, rejected under rules 1 and 6. Caveat for the merge: this is the Fund's butterfly device without the accompanying wordmark, because no file-backed version of the combined lockup is published.
